chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
In the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Ali, I bequeath to you regarding yourself certain qualities, so preserve them from me.'

Then he said: 'O Allah, support him. As for the first, it is truthfulness, and do not let a lie come out of your mouth ever. And the second is piety (al-wara'), and do not be audacious in treachery ever. And the third is fear of Allah, Mighty is His Mention, as if you see Him. And the fourth is much weeping from the fear of Allah; a thousand houses will be built for you in Paradise for every tear. And the fifth is spending your wealth and your blood for the sake of your Religion. And the sixth is adhering to my Sunnah in my Prayer, my Fasting, and my Charity.'

As for the Prayer, it is fifty Rakaat. And as for the Fasting, it is three days in the month: Thursday in the first part, Wednesday in the middle, and Thursday in the last part. And as for the Charity, it is your utmost effort, to the point that you say 'I have been excessive,' yet you have not been excessive.

And upon you is the Night Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer. And upon you is reciting the Quran in every condition. And upon you is raising your hands in your Prayer and turning them. And upon you is using the Siwak at every ablution. And upon you is adopting good morals and avoiding bad morals; if you do not do so, do not blame anyone but yourself.
ai.seo_question: What are the six qualities the Prophet bequeathed to Imam Ali in his will?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s specific bequest to Imam Ali, emphasizing six core virtues: truthfulness, piety, God-consciousness, weeping in prayer, and self-sacrifice for the faith. It provides unique jurisprudential details, such as the specific days for monthly fasting and the emphasis on the 'Prayer of Midday' (Salat al-Zawal), while linking moral excellence directly to ritual practice. This narration underscores the Shia tradition of integrating ethical conduct with precise ritual observance as a path to spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali: H 14481 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al-No’man, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said: ‘I heard Abu Abdullah say: ‘There was in the bequest of the Prophetsaww to Aliasws that hesaww said: ‘O Aliasws, Isaww hereby bequeath youasws with regards to yourselfasws of qualities, so preserve them from mesaww’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Support him<sup>asws</sup>. As for the first one is to be truthful, and do not let lies to come out from you<sup>asws</sup> ever. And the second is the piety and do not let yourself<sup>asws</sup> be treacherous ever. And the third is the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Mighty is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, as if you<sup>asws</sup> can actually see Him<sup>azwj</sup>. And the fourth is the excessive weeping for the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. There will be built for you<sup>asws</sup>, for every tear drop, a thousand houses in the Paradise. And the fifth is that your<sup>asws</sup> wealth and your<sup>asws</sup> blood is not for other than your<sup>asws</sup> Religion. And the sixth is to take to my<sup>saww</sup> Sunnah with regards to my<sup>saww</sup> Prayer, and my<sup>saww</sup> Fast, and my<sup>saww</sup> charity.

As for the Prayer, so it is of fifty Rakaat[12], and as for the Fasts, so that is for three days in the month, the Thursday in the first part of it, and the Wednesday in the middle of it, and the Thursday in the last part of it. And as for the charity, so youasws strive in it to the extent that youasws would say: ‘Iasws have been excessive’, but youasws would not have been excessive.

And it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to perform the Night Prayer, and it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to perform the Noon Prayer, and it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to perform the Noon Prayer, and it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to perform the Noon Prayer. 
And it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to recite the Quran in every condition. And it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to raise your<sup>asws</sup> hands in your<sup>asws</sup> Prayer and turn them both. And it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to brush (your<sup>asws</sup> teeth) during every ablution. And it is on you<sup>asws</sup> to observe the most excellent morals and to abstain from evil manners, for it you<sup>asws</sup> do not do it, so you<sup>asws</sup> should not blame anyone except for yourself<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 33. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al-No’man, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said: ‘I heard Abu Abdullah say: ‘

There was in the bequest of the Prophet (saww) to Ali (a.s.) that he (saww) said: ‘O Ali (a.s.), I (saww) hereby bequeath you (a.s.) with regards to yourself (a.s.) of qualities, so preserve them from me (saww)’.

Then he (saww) said: ‘Our Allah (azwj), Support him (a.s.). As for the first one is to be truthful, and do not let lies to come out from you (a.s.) ever. And the second is the piety and do not let yourself (a.s.) be treacherous ever. And the third is the fear of Allah (azwj), Mighty is His (azwj) Mention, as if you (a.s.) can actually see Him (azwj). And the fourth is the excessive weeping for the fear of Allah (azwj). There will be built for you (a.s.), for every tear drop, a thousand houses in the Paradise. And the fifth is that your (a.s.) wealth and your (a.s.) blood is not for other than your (a.s.) Religion. And the sixth is to take to my (saww) Sunnah with regards to my (saww) Prayer, and my (saww) Fast, and my (saww) charity.

As for the Prayer, so it is of fifty Rakaat, and as for the Fasts, so that is for three days in the month, the Thursday in the first part of it, and the Wednesday in the middle of it, and the Thursday in the last part of it. And as for the charity, so you (a.s.) strive in it to the extent that you (a.s.) would say: ‘I (a.s.) have been excessive’, but you (a.s.) would not have been excessive.

And it is on you (a.s.) to perform the Night Prayer, and it is on you (a.s.) to perform the Noon Prayer, and it is on you (a.s.) to perform the Noon Prayer, and it is on you (a.s.) to perform the Noon Prayer. And it is on you (a.s.) to recite the Quran in every condition. And it is on you (a.s.) to raise your (a.s.) hands in your (a.s.) Prayer and turn them both. And it is on you (a.s.) to brush (your (a.s.) teeth) during every ablution. And it is on you (a.s.) to observe the most excellent morals and to abstain from evil manners, for it you (a.s.) do not do it, so you (a.s.) should not blame anyone except for yourself (a.s.)’.
